title: On error bounds and noncritical Lagrange multipliers
summary: Critical Lagrange multipliers are known to be responsible for the potentially slow convergence of Newton-type methods, and noncriticality of a given multiplier has been tied to an error bound which estimates the distance of a primal-dual pair associated with a perturbed problem to the primal solution and the multiplier set of the unperturbed one, and is decisive for a local convergence analysis.
